title: Perfect ring complexes glue over finite principal covers
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $C\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in R$, $r\geq0$, generate the unit ideal (there are $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in R$ with $\sum_j u_jf_j=1$). Write $R_{f_j}=R[1/f_j]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and use derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. If $C\otimes_R^L R_{f_j}$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] for every $j$, then $C$ is perfect.

proof.text: Choose a complex K representing C by essential surjectivity of Q. Localization is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], and extension of scalars is therefore exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] (Mathlib ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat; colimit preservation follows from its adjunction). Mathlib mapDerivedCategory and mapDerivedCategoryFactors compute the exact functor termwise. The isomorphism mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh exhibits this functor as a left derived functor, and leftDerivedNatIso compares it with each supplied L i and counit. Transport local perfectness through this comparison and through Q(K) ≅ C to obtain perfectness of Q(K localized at f i). No site identification or K-flat resolution is needed.

source.place: Tag 066Y: passage between the complex formulation and derived scalar extension

proof.text: For each $i$, unpack [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] to choose a bounded finite-projective representative $P_i^\bullet$ of the localization. Apply [lem-pc-finite-projective-complex-free-model] over $R_{f_i}$ to replace it by a bounded-above finite-free complex. This witnesses pseudo-coherence in the sense of [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. The pseudo-coherent clause of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-localization-glue] applied to $K^\bullet$ now proves that $C$ is pseudo-coherent.

Unpack each local perfect representative P_i with strict bounds a_i and b_i. Replace these bounds by min(a_i,b_i) and max(a_i,b_i) so the interval is ordered, without any nonzero-complex assumption. Its projective terms are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. Apply the bounded-flat-model direction of [lem-pc-module-tor-amplitude-flat-model] using P_i and its derived isomorphism to the localized K. Choose a lower bound a of the finite range of local lower endpoints and an upper bound b of the finite range of upper endpoints. These bounds exist also for an empty range. Then min(a,0) ≤ max(b,0), and torAmplitudeIn.mono widens each local interval to these common bounds.

source.place: Tag 066Y proof via Tags 0658 and 0654 (lemma-tor-amplitude), bounded-flat-model implication

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tor-amplitude-principal-cover-glue] to $K^\bullet$, the given unit-ideal family, and the common bounds $a,b$ from the preceding step. This gives $H^n(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for every $R$-module $M$ and every $n\notin[a,b]$, which is finite Tor dimension over $R$.

Apply [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect] to Q(K), the global pseudo-coherence of step 2, and the global ordered Tor interval of step 4. The conclusion supplies a bounded finite-projective representative P with termwise vanishing below some c and above some d. Convert this vanishing to P.IsStrictlyGE c and P.IsStrictlyLE d, pair projectivity and finite generation of its terms, and compose Q(P) ≅ Q(K) with Q(K) ≅ C. These data are exactly [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], here the original DerivedCategory.IsPerfect predicate.
